sources.note: Nothing on stress. Secondary: Loukotka 1968 lists Mawakwa under the Mapidian group, Mavaca River, Venezuela; Aikhenvald 1999 treats Mawakwa as a possible dialect/name of Mawayana (Mapidian); the Mawayana phonology summary on Wikipedia mentions no stress.

sources.citation: von Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp. 1867. Woertersammlung Brasilianischer Sprachen (Beitraege zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, II). Leipzig: Fleischer. 'Vocabula comparata e dialectis Guyanae britanicae', pp. 311-313
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Column '9. Mawakwa' of Schomburgk's 18-language comparative table reprinted verbatim (p. 313): 16 words (sol kamu, luna kirsu, sidera wishi, terra tshimari, ignis tshikasi, aqua wune, caput unkaua, oculus ngnoso, nasus ngndewa, os ngnomiti, manus ngnkowa, pes ungeopa, arcus thseye, sagitta kengye) + numerals apaura, woaraka, tamarsi; no accent marks; p. 311 says the table is Schomburgk's (Report of the British Association for 1848 p. 97).

sources.citation: Wallace, Alfred Russel. 1853. A Narrative of Travels on the Amazon and Rio Negro. London: Reeve. Appendix 'Vocabularies of Amazonian Languages' with R. G. Latham's comparative remarks/tables (Project Gutenberg #71436)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing about Mawakwa. Latham's tables (end of appendix) give 'Mawakwa' forms for hand ngn-kowa, water wune, fire tshikase, sun kamu, moon kirsu, one apaura, taken from Schomburgk's Guiana lists. Wallace's note 'the accent shows where the stress is to be laid' applies to his own eleven Rio Negro/Uaupes vocabularies, which do not include Mawakwa.
